title: The good works of believers are not sins
source_text: IX. Igitur opera quae per Dei gratiam a fidelibus fiunt, cum vere bona & justa sint, nec revera sunt, nec sunt appellanda peccata. Quis ausit inter peccata numerare Abrahami in filio offerendo obsequium, Josephi continentiam, Eliae zelum & fervorem, & Pauli constantiam atque alacritatem in exequendo munere a Christo demandato, inter tot adversa atque pericula; aliaque virorum sanctorum egregia facta, quae Spiritus sanctus in scriptura laudat, & in exemplum aliis proponit?
pass_a_gloss: IX. Therefore the works which are done by the faithful through the grace of God, since they are truly good & just, neither are in reality, nor are to be called sins. Who would dare to number among sins Abraham's obedience in offering his son, Joseph's continence, Elijah's zeal & fervour, & Paul's constancy & eagerness in carrying out the office committed to him by Christ, amid so many adversities & dangers; & the other excellent deeds of holy men, which the Holy Spirit praises in Scripture, & sets forth as an example to others?
pass_b_english: Thesis IX. So the works believers do by God's grace are truly good and just; they are not sins and must not be called sins.

Who would dare to count as sins Abraham's obedience in offering up his son, Joseph's self-restraint, Elijah's zeal and fervour, or Paul's steadfastness and eagerness in carrying out the task Christ gave him amid so many hardships and dangers? Who would count as sins the other outstanding deeds of holy men that the Holy Spirit praises in Scripture and holds up as an example to others?
